texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 19.08.2023. 2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that on 19.08.2023 at about 12.30 p.m., the petitioner was pillion rider in motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-51-HK-9240 which was ridden by her husband Ibrahim from their house to city via Nagawara-Thanisandra Main Road when they have approached element mall in a slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules and regulations with due care and caution, at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. PY-01-B- 8555 came from opposite direction from Nagawara towards thanisandra unmind of the traffic rules and regulation, suddenly took his right turn unmindfull of the petitioner, came in high speed and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident. Due to the terrific impact, petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body. Immediately, she was shifted to Image diagnostics Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital, Bangalore, wherein she was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses, nourishment and conveyance charges. The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident she was heal and healthy and aged about 21 years, the petitioner was newly married and she was looking after her family affairs without any aid and she used to wash cloths, clean the house, cook for her family members by which she used to save a sum of Rs.15,000/- p.m. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and unable to look after the said work. Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest. 3. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent. Hence, placed exparte. Afra Mehek vs Madan Mohan A on 30 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73016241/ 2 The respondent No.2 appear through its counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending Car. Further, this respondent admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and policy was inforce as on the date of accident and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy. Further, this respondent does not admit that the driver of the offending Car and petitioner motorcycle had valid driving license to drive/ride their respective vehicles at the time of the accident. He also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.16 and examined one Vasanth Kumar as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.17 to Ex.P.19 and also examined Dr. B. Ramesh as PW.3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.20 and 21 and closed their side. On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of respondents.
texts.arguments: In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M. V. Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.
